\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter05.CorrelatedMajority}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[First marginal of a correlated sign pair]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_fst}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_fst}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.noiseKernel, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_bind, FABL.pmfExpectation_const, FABL.pmfExpectation_map, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $-1\leq\rho\leq1$, and let $X$ be uniform on the set of
sign vectors ${-1,1}^n$. Given $X$, form $Y$ by independently at each coordinate
keeping $X_i$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and replacing it by $-X_i$ otherwise. For
every real-valued function $f$ on the sign vectors, the expectation of $f(X)$ under the
resulting joint distribution of $(X,Y)$ equals its expectation under the uniform
distribution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second marginal of a correlated sign pair]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_snd}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_snd}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlatedPairPMF_map_swap, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_fst, FABL.pmfExpectation_map, FABL.uniformPMF}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $-1\leq\rho\leq1$, and let $X$ be uniform on the set of
sign vectors ${-1,1}^n$. Given $X$, form $Y$ by independently at each coordinate
keeping $X_i$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and replacing it by $-X_i$ otherwise. For
every real-valued function $f$ on the sign vectors, the expectation of $f(Y)$ under the
resulting joint distribution of $(X,Y)$ equals its expectation under the uniform
distribution.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise expectation of a linear form]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_noiseKernel_linearForm}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_noiseKernel_linearForm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.linearForm, FABL.monomial, FABL.noiseKernel, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_noiseKernel_monomial, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, let $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, and let
$a=(a_i)_{i=0}^{n-1}\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Independently in each coordinate, retain $x_i$
with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and otherwise replace it by $-x_i$, producing a random
sign vector $Y$. The expected value of the linear form $\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}a_iY_i$ is
$\rho\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}a_ix_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Correlated expectation of linear forms]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_linearForm_mul}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_linearForm_mul}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.expect_linearForm_sq, FABL.linearForm, FABL.noiseKernel, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_bind, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_map, FABL.pmfExpectation_noiseKernel_linearForm, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $-1\leq\rho\leq1$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\bbr$.
Choose $X$ uniformly from ${-1,1}^n$ and, independently at each coordinate conditional
on $X$, form $Y$ by keeping $X_i$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and flipping its sign
otherwise. Then the expectation of $(\sum_{i=1}^n a_iX_i)(\sum_{i=1}^n a_iY_i)$ is
$\rho\sum_{i=1}^n a_i^2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Normalized margin as a linear form]
\lean{FABL.normalizedMargin_eq_linearForm}
\label{FABL.normalizedMargin_eq_linearForm}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.linearForm, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{1}
For every natural number $n$ and every sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, the normalized sum
of its coordinates equals the linear form with every coefficient equal to $n^{-1/2}$:
\[\frac{1}{\sqrt n}\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{x_i}{\sqrt n}.\]
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of squared normalized coefficients]
\lean{FABL.sum_normalizedCoefficient_sq}
\label{FABL.sum_normalizedCoefficient_sq}
\leanok
\difficulty{4}
For every positive natural number $n$, the sum over the $n$ coordinates of the squares
of the coefficient $1/\sqrt n$ is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of the second coordinate]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_second_mean}
\label{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_second_mean}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlationSecondCoordinate, FABL.correlationSecondCoordinate_normalizedCorrelatedPairSum, FABL.expect_monomial, FABL.linearForm, FABL.monomial, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum, FABL.normalizedMargin_eq_linearForm, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_snd, FABL.pmfExpectation_uniformPMF_eq_expect, FABL.signValue}
\difficulty{4}
Let $-1\leq \rho\leq 1$ and let $n$ be any natural number. Under the correlated
distribution on pairs of sign vectors that chooses the first uniformly and keeps each
coordinate for the second with probability $(1+\rho)/2$, the expected second coordinate
of their normalized sum is zero.
\end{theorem}

\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_second_secondMoment}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p136-b008}

\difficulty{3}
Let $-1\leq \rho\leq 1$ and let $n$ be a positive integer. Under the correlated
distribution on pairs of sign vectors that chooses the first uniformly and keeps each
coordinate for the second with probability $(1+\rho)/2$, the expected square of the
second coordinate of their normalized sum is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Cross moment of the normalized pair sum]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_crossMoment}
\label{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_crossMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlationFirstCoordinate, FABL.correlationFirstCoordinate_normalizedCorrelatedPairSum, FABL.correlationSecondCoordinate, FABL.correlationSecondCoordinate_normalizedCorrelatedPairSum, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum, FABL.normalizedMargin_eq_linearForm, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_correlatedPairPMF_linearForm_mul, FABL.sum_normalizedCoefficient_sq}
\difficulty{3}
Let $-1\leq \rho\leq 1$ and let $n$ be a positive integer. Choose a pair of sign vectors
by taking the first uniformly at random and, independently at each coordinate, keeping
its sign for the second with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and flipping it otherwise. The
expected product of the two coordinates of their normalized sum (each coordinate sum
divided by $\sqrt n$) is $\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Moments of a correlated sign-pair sum]
\lean{FABL.exercise5_19}
\label{FABL.exercise5_19}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlationFirstCoordinate, FABL.correlationSecondCoordinate, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_crossMoment, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_first_mean, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_first_secondMoment, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_second_mean, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_second_secondMoment, FABL.pmfExpectation}
\difficulty{1}
Let $\rho\in[-1,1]$ and let $n$ be a positive integer. Choose $X$ uniformly from
$\{-1,1\}^n$; independently in each coordinate, let $Y_i=X_i$ with probability
$(1+\rho)/2$ and $Y_i=-X_i$ otherwise. For the normalized sums $S=n^{-1/2}\sum_i X_i$
and $T=n^{-1/2}\sum_i Y_i$, expectation under this joint distribution satisfies
$\mathbb{E}S=\mathbb{E}T=0$, $\mathbb{E}S^2=\mathbb{E}T^2=1$, and $\mathbb{E}(ST)=\rho$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean of a linear projection]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_projection_mean}
\label{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_projection_mean}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlationFirstCoordinate, FABL.correlationSecondCoordinate, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_first_mean, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_second_mean, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_mul_const}
\difficulty{3}
Let $-1\leq \rho\leq 1$, let $n$ be any natural number, and let $t$ be any point of the
plane. For a pair of sign vectors sampled by choosing the first uniformly and keeping
each coordinate for the second with probability $(1+\rho)/2$, the expected inner product
of their normalized sum with $t$ is zero.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Second moment of a linear projection]
\lean{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_projection_secondMoment}
\label{FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_projection_secondMoment}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.CorrelationPlane, FABL.correlatedPairPMF, FABL.correlationFirstCoordinate, FABL.correlationQuadraticForm, FABL.correlationSecondCoordinate, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_crossMoment, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_first_secondMoment, FABL.normalizedCorrelatedPairSum_second_secondMoment, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_add, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_mul_const}
\difficulty{4}
Let $-1\leq \rho\leq 1$, let $n$ be a positive integer, and let $t=(t_1,t_2)$ be any
point of the plane. For a pair of sign vectors sampled by choosing the first uniformly
and keeping each coordinate for the second with probability $(1+\rho)/2$, the expected
square of the inner product of their normalized sum with $t$ is $t_1^2+2\rho
t_1t_2+t_2^2$.
\end{theorem}
